steps.name: QC and filtering of raw counts
steps.question: Do the 6 liver samples (3 treated, 3 control) in counts.csv show adequate library size, gene detection, and sample-sample correlation to proceed to differential expression, and which low-count genes should be filtered before modeling?
acceptance_criteria: Library size and gene detection rate reported per sample for all 6 samples
Sample correlation / PCA computed on variance-stabilized counts to check for outliers or unexpected clustering by condition
Low-count genes (e.g., rowSum or rowMean threshold appropriate for n=3 per group) flagged for filtering, with the number of genes retained out of the original 12000 reported
Metadata condition column confirmed to align 3 treated vs 3 control against the count matrix column order

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples using DESeq2 on the STAR/featureCounts raw counts, after low-count filtering from T1S1?
acceptance_criteria: DESeqDataSet built directly from raw integer counts and the metadata condition column (control as reference level)
Median-of-ratios size factor normalization applied (appropriate for featureCounts gene-level counts, no transcript-length offset needed)
Negative binomial GLM fit with Wald test for the treated-vs-control contrast
Independent filtering applied and log2 fold changes shrunk with apeglm (or ashr as fallback) for stable ranking
Full results table (gene, baseMean, log2FoldChange, shrunk LFC, p-value, padj) exported, with count of genes at padj < 0.05
Caveat stated: n=3 per group limits power to detect subtle effects and precludes robust outlier-sample exclusion decisions

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the treated-vs-control signature
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples (from T1S2)?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis run on the padj<0.05 DE gene set (or a stated alternative threshold if too few genes pass) against a human pathway gene-set collection
Pre-ranked GSEA run on the full gene list ranked by the DESeq2 shrunk log2FoldChange (or signed -log10(p) x sign(LFC)) against the same gene sets

Uses the WikiPathways human gene sets (HGNC symbols) available in the reference store; if this resource is unavailable at run time, the step must report that gap explicitly rather than silently skipping enrichment
Enriched pathways reported with adjusted p-values (BH), normalized enrichment scores for GSEA, and leading-edge genes for top hits
Gene symbol matching between DESeq2 result IDs and WikiPathways HGNC symbols verified/harmonized before testing

plan.title: Liver drug treatment vs control DESeq2 DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is raw integer gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples) from STAR/featureCounts for a human liver drug-treatment study, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. This is a standard bulk RNA-seq design well suited to DESeq2's negative-binomial GLM, which is validated for STAR/featureCounts-derived counts (no transcript-level offsets needed, unlike Salmon/kallisto outputs that require tximport). Track 1 runs QC/normalization then DESeq2 differential expression with independent filtering and effect-size shrinkage (apeglm) to get a stable, ranked gene list. Track 2 takes that ranked list into pathway enrichment (ORA + GSEA) against the WikiPathways human gene sets available in the reference store, giving biological interpretation of the treated-vs-control signature. No translational/PK/safety data are present in this dataset, so no such steps are added.
